original_question: Is every cubic solid brick odd-intercyclic? Here a graph is odd-intercyclic when any two odd cycles in it have a vertex in common, and the question asks whether every 3-regular solid brick must satisfy that odd-cycle intersection property.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.15 in §1.5: every cubic solid brick is odd-intercyclic. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1705.09428))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the exact conjecture the paper states, rather than drifting to the broader surrounding problem of characterizing all solid bricks. It also states the odd-intercyclic property correctly as the requirement that any two odd cycles have a common vertex. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1705.09428))
missing_details: The official target is Conjecture 1.15 in §1.5, so it helps to name it explicitly rather than present it as an informal side question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1705.09428))
The paper works throughout with loopless graphs; that ambient assumption is implicit in your draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1705.09428))

To make the question fully stand-alone, brick should be unpacked in the paper’s sense: a nonbipartite matching covered graph with no nontrivial tight cuts, where matching covered means connected and every edge lies in some perfect matching. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1705.09428))

To make the question fully stand-alone, solid should be unpacked in the paper’s sense: a solid brick is precisely a brick with no nontrivial separating cuts, and a separating cut is one whose two cut-contractions are both matching covered. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1705.09428))

The nearby context records that the converse direction is already known: every odd-intercyclic brick is solid, by the discussion immediately following Theorem 1.13. So the open problem is specifically the reverse implication in the cubic-brick setting. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1705.09428))

Your wording should avoid adding extra hypotheses not present in the conjecture, such as simplicity, planarity, or nonplanarity; Conjecture 1.15 is stated for cubic solid bricks in general. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1705.09428))
refined_question: Let G be a loopless cubic graph. Assume that G is a brick, meaning that G is a connected nonbipartite graph in which every edge belongs to some perfect matching and G has no nontrivial tight cuts, where a cut is tight if every perfect matching meets it in exactly one edge. If G is also solid, equivalently if G has no nontrivial separating cuts (a cut is separating if both of its cut-contractions are matching covered), must G be odd-intercyclic; that is, must every two odd cycles of G share a vertex? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1705.09428))
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s exact intent: it targets Conjecture 1.15 in §1.5. I only sharpened it by reinstating the local definitions that the paper assumes in the surrounding context—matching covered graphs from §1.1, separating cuts from §1.3.3, bricks and tight cuts from §1.4.1, and solid bricks plus the odd-intercyclic definition from §1.5. I did not broaden it to Unsolved Problem 1.14 or to other neighboring characterization problems. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1705.09428))
